question: What distinguishes the apprehension of objects according to manifest and unmanifest practice?
premises: Apprehension is distinguished by manifest and unmanifest character
This distinction arises from practice with objects
The result corresponds appropriately to each case
inference: Practice with objects yields an apprehension differentiated by degrees of manifestness, each in its proper way
plain_english: Distinguished by manifest and unmanifest character, from the practice of objects, in each case as appropriate,
